title: Willow Porch Cottage
lesson: A low gable, deep porch and asymmetrical garden make a modest house inviting.
fit: The porch is centred on the door; a tree frames the left edge and a bench faces the garden.
avoid: Do not put a lamppost in the small front garden or cover the porch approach with planting.

title: Marigold Market Court
lesson: Two different shops and a produce stall share one pedestrian court.
fit: Keep the middle court open; repeat cream trim but vary roof colour and storefront width.
avoid: Do not mirror every detail or fill the court with furniture.

title: Aster Museum Pavilion
lesson: Symmetry, a columned portico and a stepped pediment establish a civic focal point.
fit: Pair lamps beside the central approach; reserve the central axis for the portico.
avoid: Avoid striped shop awnings and random bright accents on the classical front.

title: Cinder Bay Fire Station
lesson: A wide vehicle portal, hose tower and red/white bands make the function readable.
fit: The vehicle apron stays empty; the tower sits behind one edge of the garage.
avoid: Do not put trees, benches or stairs in the vehicle exit.

title: Sunbeam Learning Courtyard
lesson: A classroom wing, clock block and courtyard create a small campus with an obvious entrance.
fit: Use the courtyard for gathering and the quieter side for a garden bench.
avoid: Keep trees outside the classroom window band and the entrance axis.

title: Seabreeze Community Clinic
lesson: A low horizontal wing, a taller glazed reception and a clear medical marker distinguish a clinic.
fit: A broad level approach leads to reception; a quiet planted side court balances the sign.
avoid: No stairs at the main entrance; the cross is a functional identifier, not scattered decoration.

title: Copperworks Repair Yard
lesson: Repeated glazed roof bays and a separate utility stack communicate a workshop.
fit: Keep the working yard sparse, use darker materials low down, and group equipment to one side.
avoid: Do not use domestic flower boxes or a ceremonial entrance.

title: Hawthorn Halt
lesson: An elongated platform, shelter and ticket house establish direction and passenger circulation.
fit: The canopy runs along the platform; benches face the implied track edge at the front.
avoid: Do not put furnishings in the platform edge strip; no rolling-stock clearance is claimed.

title: Red Barn Farmstead
lesson: A tall barn, smaller granary, fenced yard and crop patch make a working cluster.
fit: Leave a broad barn approach; use fences to describe the yard rather than enclose every edge.
avoid: Avoid urban paving and lampposts; the crops belong in rows away from vehicle access.

title: Greywatch Gatehouse
lesson: Paired crenellated towers flank an open arch and a clear defended approach.
fit: Keep the gate visually dominant; use sparse green at the foot of heavy stone walls.
avoid: Do not add cottage windows everywhere or block the gate with a tree.

title: Hazelbridge Village
lesson: A tall timber inn and a smaller smithy frame a shared working square.
fit: Use shared timber/stone colours but different roof heights; put the stall on the square edge.
avoid: Avoid identical paired façades and modern lighting.

title: Jade Terrace Pavilion
lesson: Three diminishing roof tiers and repeated red columns establish a vertical ceremonial rhythm.
fit: Keep a clear central stair and frame the entrance with paired planters.
avoid: Do not describe this stylized pavilion as an accurate reconstruction of a particular culture or monument.

title: Fernlight Glasshouse
lesson: A transparent envelope and repeated dark mullions let planting become the interior focus.
fit: Keep dense plants inside the glazed volume and quiet paths outside.
avoid: Do not fill the roof with opaque decoration or block every view through the glazing.

title: Canopy Field Station
lesson: An elevated hut, visible support trunk, access stair and surrounding canopy form a vertical nature scene.
fit: Let the trunk remain visible below the platform; foliage frames the hut instead of intersecting it.
avoid: Never float a hut in leaves; the platform needs a continuous load path and access.

title: Saltwind Light and Keeper Cottage
lesson: A slender banded tower and low cottage balance a waterside composition.
fit: The beacon is the skyline focus; the cottage stays lower and the water remains uncluttered.
avoid: Do not imply a working Fresnel lens or motor; this is a static architectural study.

title: Snowbell Alpine Lodge
lesson: A steep snow roof, warm timber walls and sheltered porch create a winter retreat.
fit: Keep snow as broad roof/ground masses; warm accents cluster around the entrance.
avoid: Do not scatter white studs indiscriminately or place foliage through the roof.

title: Moonflower Observatory
lesson: Offset tower masses, a pointed roof and restrained magical colour create a fantasy silhouette.
fit: Use the high spire as the focal feature; keep magical accents small and repeat the same palette.
avoid: Do not use arbitrary floating geometry or add a different bright colour to every tier.

title: Selene Research Outpost
lesson: Two low habitats, a linking passage and a separate landing pad form a coherent functional compound.
fit: Use white hulls, dark equipment and localized blue glazing; beacons define the landing edge.
avoid: Keep terrestrial landscaping and Victorian lamps out; the dish is static, not an articulated mechanism.

title: Three Rivers Skyline
lesson: Three different tower silhouettes around a shared plinth demonstrate massing at a declared small scale.
fit: Use tiny repeated window bands and broad quiet plinths; tower spacing is part of the composition.
avoid: Never mix full minifigure doors, trees or lampposts into this scene.

title: Mesa Crossing Trading Post
lesson: A false-front shop, boardwalk and small stable establish a frontier settlement.
fit: Timber porches and a dusty open yard belong here; keep the false front above the lower roof.
avoid: Do not rely on lettering alone to distinguish the building from a modern shop.

title: Sunwell Desert Sanctuary
lesson: A stepped platform, open colonnade and paired pylons express an archaeological adventure setting.
fit: Use a clear ceremonial axis and sparse warm stone accents; leave the ruins visually open.
avoid: Do not invent historical accuracy or place unrelated medieval/gothic decoration on the sanctuary.
